You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC offset divider panels extend marker rays and project lines', content='''Observed task-d3b18386 with six demos. Rule: a large uniform-background grid has two same-color straight divider/border segments on opposite sides, parallel and offset along their length. A distinct marker color (various demos: 0, 5, 7, 8, 9) appears on one side. The pattern is projected into the opposite panel by the offset between divider segments, and source markers become color 4. For each source marker row/column, extend the marker color from the nearby border side up to (but not including) the marker; replace marker with 4. In the corresponding translated row/column in the opposite panel, fill the full span from one edge to the opposite divider with marker color. Preserve divider lines, other cells, and background. Orientation generalizes: horizontal divider segments cause vertical displacement/projection; vertical segments cause horizontal runs/projection. Validate exact offset and edge extents from divider segment endpoints. Confirmed test: left color-2 vertical segment rows1..8 at col0, right segment rows9..16 at col19 (offset +8); color-5 markers at (r,c)=(1,16),(3,7),(4,6),(5,5),(7,4),(8,16). Each source row had 5 filled from c1 to c-1, marker changed to 4; translated rows 9,11,12,13,15,16 were filled color 5 across c0..18, with right border col19 preserved. Important lesson from failed hypotheses: do NOT fill source marker rows past marker toward the far edge; source ray runs from adjacent divider toward the marker. Translated rows include the background-side edge cell (e.g. col0) but stop before the opposite colored divider. Demo5 verifies vertical arrangement with markers in lower panel projecting upward; demo4 verifies same rule rotated.''', path='arc_tasks', metadata={'task_id':'task-d3b18386','version':1}, global_=True)
print(entry)
